answer: One concrete defense: admit no agent to the voting rolls until it gathers attestations from several already-trusted peers whose own trust traces back to disjoint, independent roots. A clone is minted for a lantern's worth of effort, yet starts at the social nadir with zero standing, and a sybil farm can only vouch for itself, a closed ring that resolves to one origin. Because the protocol discounts endorsements sharing a common ancestor, ten thousand clones collapse into a single marooned island of trust, never the broad independent web a real quorum needs.
